generation.hypothesis: The single intervention that could improve dynamic strength-ductility performance in high-entropy alloys is the introduction of lattice distortion through the addition of elements with large atomic radii, such as Zr.
generation.intervention: Addition of Zr or other elements with large atomic radii
generation.conditions: Room temperature to high temperatures, various strain rates
generation.mechanism: The introduction of lattice distortion through the addition of elements with large atomic radii, such as Zr, can lead to enhanced strength and plasticity in high-entropy alloys. This is because the lattice distortion can create multiple slip systems and high flow stress, resulting in improved dynamic strength-ductility performance. (Derived from materials-science principles and records PMC9506522, PMC7311485, and PMC11310445)
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved dynamic strength-ductility performance, with increased yield strength and ductility
generation.baseline: As-cast or wrought high-entropy alloy without lattice distortion
generation.boundary: The improvement in dynamic strength-ductility performance is expected to occur at room temperature to high temperatures, and at various strain rates
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of improvement in dynamic strength-ductility performance may vary depending on the specific composition and processing conditions of the high-entropy alloy

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing of high-entropy alloys with and without lattice distortion at various temperatures and strain rates
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the introduction of lattice distortion does not lead to improved dynamic strength-ductility performance, the hypothesis is falsified.

Lattice distortion enabling enhanced strength and plasticity in high entropy intermetallic alloy

Abstract: AbstractIntermetallic alloys have traditionally been characterized by their inherent brittleness due to their lack of sufficient slip systems and absence of strain hardening. However, here we developed a single-phase B2 high-entropy intermetallic alloy that is both strong and plastic. Unlike conventional intermetallics, this high-entropy alloy features a highly distorted crystalline lattice with complex chemical order, leading to multiple slip systems and high flow stress. In addition, the alloy exhibits a dynamic hardening mechanism triggered by dislocation gliding that preserves its strength across a wide range of temperatures. As a result, this high-entropy intermetallic circumvents precipitous thermal softening, with extensive plastic flows even at high homologous temperatures, outperforming a variety of both body-centered cubic and B2 alloys. Evidence of Inverse Hall-Petch Behavior and Low Friction and Wear in High Entropy Alloys

Abstract: AbstractWe present evidence of inverse Hall-Petch behavior for a single-phase high entropy alloy (CoCrFeMnNi) in ultra-high vacuum and show that it is associated with low friction coefficients (~0.3). Grain size measurements by STEM validate a recently proposed dynamic amorphization model that accurately predicts grain size-dependent shear strength in the inverse Hall-Petch regime. Wear rates in the initially soft (coarse grained) material were shown to be remarkably low (~10–6 mm3/N-m), the lowest for any HEA tested in an inert environment where oxidation and the formation of mixed metal-oxide films is mitigated. The combined high wear resistance and low friction are linked to the formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer. The dynamic amorphization model was also used to predict an average high angle grain boundary energy (0.87 J/m2). This value was used to explain cavitation-induced nanoporosity found in the highly deformed surface layer, a phenomenon that has been linked to superplasticity.Subject terms: Structural materials, Structural properties

Remarkable Enhanced Mechanical Properties of TiAlCrNbV Medium-Entropy Alloy with Zr Additions

Abstract: Most medium entropy alloys (MEAs) exhibit excellent mechanical properties, but their applications are limited because of their high density. This study explores a series of lightweight nonequiatomic Ti65(AlCrNbV)35-xZrx (x = 3, 5, 7, and 10) MEAs with a low density, high strength, and high ductility. To achieve solid solution strengthening, Zr with a large atomic radius was used. In addition, various thermomechanical treatment parameters were adopted to further improve the MEAs’ mechanical properties. The density of the MEAs was revealed to be approximately 5 g/cm3, indicating that they were lightweight. Through an X-ray diffraction analysis, the MEAs were revealed to have a single body-centered cubic structure not only in the as-cast state but also after thermomechanical treatment. In terms of mechanical properties, all the as-cast MEAs with Zr additions achieved excellent performance (>1000 MPa tensile yield strength and 20% tensile ductility).
